title: Similar right triangles: carry a ratio or a side across
subtitle: Right triangles and trigonometry · 12 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **12 of the official questions in Right triangles and trigonometry are this one** — 1 Easy, 1 Medium, 10 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:

- The problem says two triangles are similar and lists which vertices correspond, or the figure has parallel segments, or a perpendicular altitude dropped inside a right triangle, which makes nested triangles.
- You get a trig value or sides in one triangle and are asked about the other.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Use the correspondence to match equal angles; congruent angles have identical sin, cos, and tan.
- 2) Compute the trig ratio in whichever triangle has the known sides (use Pythagoras for a missing one), then apply it at the corresponding angle in the other triangle.
- 3) For a length, use that ratio or the scale factor together with the one length you know in the target triangle.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Not much help, because the work is matching corresponding parts, which you can't enter as a formula.
At most, you can solve the final proportion or Pythagorean step by graphing, or convert a fraction answer to a decimal.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You match vertices by where they sit in the picture instead of by the stated correspondence, so you use the wrong angle's ratio.
Or you assume the scale factor changes the trig value, when similar triangles keep it the same.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You match vertices by where they sit in the picture instead of by the stated correspondence, so you use the wrong angle's ratio.
